Super lamp

Martine Bedin’s table lamp on wheels: a blue half-disc with six bulbs in colored collars.

Source
V&A: Super Lamp (M.1-2011)
Creator
Martine Bedin (designer); Fausto Celati (maker)
Made
ca. 1977 and 1981, as the V&A records them; the V&A example is the 1981 prototype
Style
Memphis (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Playful, toy-like, cheerful, postmodern
Evidence
Downloaded the museum’s published image (843 px wide) from the V&A IIIF server to a private scratchpad and inspected it with the Read tool on 2026-09-25. No image is stored in the catalogue.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A says the Super lamp was among Bedin’s contributions to the first Memphis year (1981). Its example is the initial prototype, shown at the first Memphis exhibition at the gallery Arc 74 in 1981. V&A record.

The physical description: painted sheet steel, two stamped semicircular halves painted blue, six light sockets in steel collars of different colors along the curve, and four steel wheels with rubber tyres. V&A record.

The V&A notes that Bedin worked mainly on lighting and graphic design for Memphis and introduced Nathalie Du Pasquier to the group. V&A record.

Observed

  • The body is a glossy navy half-circle standing on its flat edge.
  • Six bare bulbs stick out along the curve in collars of red, lime, yellow, light blue, green, and pink.
  • Four black rubber wheels make it look like a pull toy.
  • The background is plain white, so the colors read as separate dots around the arc.

Why it belongs

The lamp combines a pull toy, a rainbow, and a sunrise. The ring of colored collars on one dark shape is a small version of the Memphis palette.

Borrow

Place a row of small, differently colored elements along one bold dark curve.

Add toy cues such as wheels or handles to domestic objects or interface elements.
